record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can MARL be used as a heuristic for learning causal structure by rewarding an agent for choosing actions that increase knowledge useful for causal structure learning, including learning the direction of causality, and how should the resulting causal model be used for identification and planning?

evidence.quote: As in model-based (MA)RL, it may be of interest to ﬁrst learn a causal model and then use it for identiﬁcation and planning. Recent causality literature usually frames this as causal discovery.

This presents interesting opportunities for research in MARL where, for example, MARL could be used as a heuristic for learning direction of causality by rewarding an agent for correctly choosing actions so as to increase knowledge useful for structure learning.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) setting in which a collection of agents interact with a shared environment whose underlying data-generating process is described by an unknown structural causal model (SCM). An SCM consists of a directed acyclic graph G = (V, E) over a set of endogenous variables V, together with structural assignments X_v = f_v(Pa_G(v), U_v) for each v ∈ V, where Pa_G(v) denotes the parents of v in G and U_v are independent exogenous noise variables. Agents may perform interventions do(X_S = x_S) on subsets S ⊆ V of variables by selecting actions, and observe the resulting samples from the interventional distribution P^{do(X_S = x_S)}.

Design and analyze a MARL framework with the following properties:

(a) Specify a reward function r_t for each agent that incentivizes the selection of intervention-actions which maximally increase the agents' knowledge of the causal structure G, including the orientation of edges (i.e., the direction of causality among variables). The reward should be expressible in terms of an information-theoretic or statistical criterion (for example, expected information gain about edges, or reduction of posterior entropy over the Markov-equivalence class of G) computable from the agents' interaction history.

(b) Prove convergence (or characterize the asymptotic behavior) of the joint policy under this reward to a policy whose induced data distribution permits consistent identification of G (up to its interventional equivalence class) from the agents' experience.

(c) Given the learned causal model Ĝ, formulate a procedure for using Ĝ for (i) identification of interventional and counterfactual quantities of interest, and (ii) planning of subsequent agent policies that optimize a downstream task reward, and provide guarantees on the sub-optimality of the resulting plan relative to plans computed with the true SCM, as a function of the structural-learning error.

Determine whether such a framework can be constructed, and provide either a concrete algorithm with the above guarantees or an impossibility result.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction at the interface of MARL and causal discovery. Searches reveal active recent work on causal RL and active causal discovery (e.g., reward-driven intervention selection for structure learning), but no published result provides a complete MARL-based heuristic with convergence guarantees and downstream identification/planning bounds as posed. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including using MARL as a heuristic for causal structure learning.
status_evidence.claim: The question is identified as an open research problem in a review of causal MARL.
